diagram_math_checks.evidence: def-homological-double-complex defines h_{i,j}:C_{i,j}->C_{i-1,j} and v_{i,j}:C_{i,j}->C_{i,j-1}. All 9 displayed objects have i,j in {0,1,2}; all 6 h arrows point left, and all 6 v arrows point down with these exact domains/codomains. Omitted negative-index objects are zero; the grid explicitly continues upward and right.

Each of the 4 visible squares has paths C_{i,j}->C_{i-1,j-1} given by h_{i,j-1}v_{i,j} and v_{i-1,j}h_{i,j}, for i,j in {1,2}. Their sum is zero by def-homological-double-complex and the theorem Given, so the caption explicitly states anticommutation rather than commutativity.

def-row-and-column-filtrations-of-a-first-quadrant-double-complex selects original vertical index j<=s. Hence Frow_1 retains rows 0 and 1, its quotient by Frow_0 selects row 1, and generally E0_{p,q}=C_{q,p}; h fixes row p while v lowers it. This is exactly theorem proof step 1.1.

Proof step 2.1 establishes d1[x]=[vx] on Hh_q(C_{*,p}) with no additional sign because d=h+v; hv=-vh preserves horizontal cycles and boundaries. The displayed arrows therefore have domains E1_{2,q}->E1_{1,q}->E1_{0,q} and bidegree (-1,0). Step 3.1 gives v_* squared zero and E2_{p,q}=Hv_p(Hh_q(C)); prose explicitly states upward continuation before describing homology at arbitrary p. The rigorous proof remains unchanged and independent of the figures.
